summary.text: A 73-year-old white man from Bavaria with no known relevant preexisting medical conditions was admitted to the emergency department in early March 2021 after a 5-day history of chills, productive cough with yellow sputum, shortness of breath at rest and lower limb pain. Examination showed fever, purulent conjunctivitis of the right eye and a fresh, non-inflamed wound on the distal left thigh sustained during forestry work about 10 days earlier; a possible recent tick bite was reported.

Initial laboratory tests showed creatinine 6.77 mg/dl, eGFR 8 ml/minute/1.73 m^(2) and CRP 306 mg/l, with proteinuria, hematuria and enlarged kidneys, and emergency dialysis was started. Chest imaging showed opacities and, on CT, bilateral consolidations; empirical piperacillin/tazobactam with clarithromycin gave minimal response. A low-titer pANCA with negative MPO- and PR3-ANCA was found, and a renal biopsy showed pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis.

Intravenous corticosteroids and one plasmapheresis session were started and pulse cyclophosphamide was scheduled, but blood cultures then grew F. tularensis, later confirmed as subspecies holarctica with IgM and IgG serology. Cyclophosphamide was withheld, corticosteroids were tapered and stopped, and antibiotics were switched to intravenous ciprofloxacin plus ceftriaxone, with improvement. Seven dialysis sessions were given, dialysis was discontinued after a trial withdrawal, and he was discharged home on day 24.

Low-dose oral corticosteroids were reintroduced to support renal recovery and were fully tapered over the following months, with clinical remission and full recovery. At 4-year follow-up the patient remained asymptomatic with normalized inflammatory markers and renal function, and no recurrence was observed.
